context.zh: 鎮北姚彊率郡人數千，與姚難陣於涇上，以距鎮惡。
context.idiomatic: Yao Qiang, General Who Guards the North, led several thousand men of the commandery and formed ranks with Yao Nan on the Jing River to resist Wang Zhen’e.
context.literal: Yao Qiang, General Who Guards the North, led several thousand men of the commandery and formed ranks with Yao Nan on the Jing River to resist Wang Zhen’e.

context.zh: 鎮惡遣毛德祖擊彊，大敗，彊戰死，難遁還長安。
context.idiomatic: Wang Zhen’e sent Mao Dezu against Yao Qiang. Qiang’s force was routed, and Qiang died in battle. Yao Nan fled back to Chang’an.
context.literal: Zhen'e sent Mao Dezu to strike Qiang, greatly defeated him; Qiang died in battle; Nan fled back to Chang'an.

context.zh: 鎮惡夾渭進兵，破姚丕於渭橋。
context.idiomatic: Wang Zhen’e advanced along both banks of the Wei and defeated Yao Pi at Wei Bridge.
context.literal: Zhen'e advanced troops on both sides of the Wei, defeated Yao Pi at Wei Bridge.

context.zh: 泓自逍遙園赴之，逼水地狹，因丕之敗，遂相踐而退。
context.idiomatic: Yao Hong came from Xiaoyao Garden to help Yao Pi. The ground was narrow against the river, and when Pi was defeated the men trampled one another as they retreated.
context.literal: Hong went from Free-Roam Garden to aid him; pressed by water, ground narrow, because of Pi's defeat, they trampled each other in retreat.

context.zh: 鎮惡入自平朔門，泓與姚裕等數百騎出奔于石橋。
context.idiomatic: Wang Zhen’e entered through Pingshuo Gate. Yao Hong, Yao Yu and the others fled with several hundred horsemen to Stone Bridge.
context.literal: Zhen'e entered from Pingshuo Gate; Hong with Yao Yu and several hundred horse fled out toward Stone Bridge.

context.zh: 贊夜率諸軍，將會泓于石橋，王師已固諸門，贊軍不得入，眾皆驚散。
context.idiomatic: That night Yao Zan led the armies out to join Hong at Stone Bridge. The Jin army already held all the gates. Zan’s army could not enter, and his men scattered in alarm.
context.literal: Zan by night led all armies, planning to join Hong at Stone Bridge; the royal army had already secured all gates; Zan's army could not enter; the host all startled and scattered.

context.zh: 其子佛念，年十一，謂泓曰：「晉人將逞其欲，終必不全，願自裁決。」
context.idiomatic: His eleven-year-old son Fonian said to Hong, “The men of Jin will have their way. In the end there will surely be no escape. Death by one’s own hand would be better.”
context.literal: His eleven-year-old son Fonian said to Hong, “The men of Jin will have their way. In the end there will surely be no escape. Death by one’s own hand would be better.”

context.idiomatic: Hong took his wife and children to the gate of the Jin camp and surrendered.
context.literal: Hong led wife and children to the camp gate and surrendered.

context.zh: 贊率宗室子弟百餘人亦降於裕，裕盡殺之，余宗遷於江南。
context.idiomatic: Yao Zan also surrendered to Liu Yu, leading more than a hundred younger men of the imperial clan. Liu Yu killed them all. The rest of the clan was moved south of the Yangtze.
context.literal: Zan led more than a hundred sons and nephews of the imperial clan also to surrender to Yu; Yu killed them all; the rest of the clan was moved south of the Yangzi.

context.zh: 史臣曰：自長江徙禦，化龍創業，巨寇乘機而未寧，戎馬交馳而不息，晦重氛於六漠，鼓洪流於八際，天未厭亂，凶旅實繁。
context.idiomatic: The court historian says: Ever since the imperial court moved to the Yangtze and the prince of the dragon prophecy founded his dynasty there, great raiders have seized their opportunity and refused to be still. Warhorses have galloped to and fro without rest. Dense darkness shrouded the six reaches of the world, and great floods surged to its eight limits. Heaven had not yet tired of disorder, and violent armies were many indeed.
